<!-- Generated by Kora's design director. This is the design decision the site was built
     from. Business: FACIALS BY VANESSA CT SKIN JOURNEY! -->

# DESIGN.md — FACIALS BY VANESSA CT SKIN JOURNEY!

archetype: modern-advisory
rationale: Vanessa sells a plan rather than a pitch, and her clients return for her candour and her command of melanin-rich skin, so modern-advisory sets every appointment out plainly, with what it is, how long it takes and what it costs, the way a good adviser lays out a recommendation; the warm ground comes from her own brand cream and is set entirely in sans, so it never drifts into the cream-and-serif default.
interaction_level: L2

personality: [candid, assured, warm, exact]

typography:
  display: "Roboto"
  body: "Roboto"
  scale: 1.333
  notes: >
    One family in two weights, held strictly.
    Headings: Roboto 300 (Light), tracking -0.02em.
    Body: Roboto 400 at 18px on desktop and 17px on mobile, line-height 1.6, measure capped near 68ch.
    Steps: h1 4.2rem, h2 3.16rem, h3 1.78rem, h4 1.33rem.
    Prices and durations are figures, not body text. Set them in Roboto 300 with tabular numerals: h3 size in lists, h1 size in the hero facts and the journey band.
    Eyebrows: 12px uppercase, letter-spaced 0.12em, in muted.
    Buttons: 400 at 15px.
    Nothing is heavier than 400. Hierarchy comes from size and space, not weight.
    Service names stay verbatim with their capitals, so the copy around them must stay quiet.

palette:
  primary: "#a87a2c"
  secondary: "#f6f1e8"
  accent: "#2a2116"
  ground: "#fcfaf6"
  surface: "#efe5d4"
  ink: "#1e170f"
  muted: "#6b5a45"
  border: "#ddd0ba"
  application: >
    Each brand colour has one structural job.
    Accent #2a2116 carries the deep bands: the hero block, the journey band and the footer. Text on these bands is secondary cream, at 14:1. Accent is also the fill for every primary button.
    Primary gold #a87a2c is the structural mark. It carries the journey rule, the oversized figures, thin top rules on bands and link underlines. It measures 3.7:1 on ground and 4.1:1 on accent, so use it only at display size or for non-text marks. Never set body text, captions or small labels in gold or on a gold fill.
    Secondary #f6f1e8 forms full-width tint bands that alternate with the ground.
    Surface #efe5d4 is the one raised step, used for the FAQ and the booking form.
    Ink #1e170f is her umber accent pushed down until it reads as text. Muted #6b5a45 holds 6.3:1 on ground and 5.3:1 on surface.
    Links are set in ink with a gold underline. Form states use a deep green #2f6b45 for success and a brick #9a3b2a for errors. No other hues.
    Why these neutrals belong to her: every one is drawn from her bronze-and-umber family rather than a grey ramp, so the page stays warm like skin and amber oil, not clinical.

composition:
  whitespace: balanced
  photography: supporting
  card_usage: none
  mobile: >
    The hero image sits above the text block at 4:5, never behind it, and the headline drops to 2.6rem.
    The three hero facts stack as full-width rows separated by hairlines.
    The journey band turns vertical, with the gold rule running down the left edge and each stage hanging off it.
    In service rows, price and duration drop beneath the name on their own baseline.
    Hours lead with today's line set large.
    A slim accent "Book Appointment" bar is pinned to the bottom on mobile only. It is inset from the right so it never covers the accessibility widget's corner.
    The gallery becomes a free-scrolling horizontal strip, cropped at the right edge.

composition: >
  Her visitors arrive having tried "so many products" and having been brushed off elsewhere,
  often by people who did not understand dark skin. So the page wins on being believed, not on mood.
  Say plainly what she does and whose skin she understands, and let her clients make that case in
  their own words before the page asks for anything.
  Being straight about cost is the same argument as "she does not push products". Every price and
  duration therefore sits in plain sight, and nothing hides behind a "more" link.
  The essential-oils atmosphere copy is held back. She wins on judgement and candour, not on candles.

sections:
  - id: hero
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Say in one breath what this is and whose skin she understands.
      The headline is the tagline: "Facials in Hartford, designed around your skin."
      Beside it sits the single strongest gallery photograph of the work or the treatment room. The builder picks it from what the images actually show. The two logo files are never used as hero imagery.
      Three facts are set as large gold figures on the accent block: 9 years in Hartford, from $95, virtual or in the studio.
      The only action is the accent "Book Appointment" button, which links to booking.html.
      The logo sits with the business name exactly as written.
  - id: reviews
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Let five named clients prove the two things that set her apart: she understands Black and dark skin, and she never pushes products.
      Pull one quote out at display size: either pree dreams' "My skin has NEVER glowed before" or Viola Odenya's "does not push any products".
      Set the rest as plain attributed text.
      Keep quotes and author names verbatim. No star graphics, no aggregate count, and no reviewer profile photos.
  - id: offerings
    priority: essential
    show: "all 9 — name, price and duration only, grouped under her three category names; each row links to its own service page, and the section links to services.html"
    intent: >
      Make every appointment's cost and length legible at a glance, so nothing feels hidden.
      Label the section "Services", never "Menu".
      ANTI-ACNE FACIAL TREATMENT has no price in the content: show its 60 minutes and no price.
      MICRODERMABRASION has no stated duration: show its $230 only.
  - id: process
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      This is the one distinctive moment: the Skin Journey drawn as a real sequence on a gold rule, with the figures set large.
      01 — VIRTUAL SKIN JOURNEY CONSULTATION ($165, 60 min): photos and intake, a video call, then a written step-by-step plan.
      02 — Virtual Skin Journey Follow-up ($95, 30 min): how the skin responded, adjusted one change at a time.
      03 — In-studio treatment, when the plan needs hands-on work such as extractions or a peel.
      Numbering is earned here because the order is her method.
      State nothing about how this sequence is required or priced as a package, because the content does not say.
  - id: story
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: >
      Put a name and a stance to the practice.
      Her name appears exactly as given: VANESSA GORDON - MCFARLENE.
      She has spent nine years in Hartford, working alone.
      Lead with her own line: "My job is to get you the right plan, not to pressure you at checkout." Note her care with melanin-rich skin.
      Write in the first person, as one person. Never "our team".
  - id: gallery
    priority: supporting
    show: "7 of 8 — every gallery image except the one used in the hero"
    intent: >
      Give a quiet visual sense of the work and the room.
      Never caption images as before/after or as named treatments, because the content does not say what each one shows.
  - id: offers
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: >
      State her current note once, calmly, as a single line near the booking action:
      "Limited Availability — CALENDAR IS FILLING UP FOR OCTOBER- BOOK NOW!"
      No marquee and no countdown.
  - id: faq
    priority: supporting
    show: "8 of 63 — the general practical questions only (preparation, aftercare, payment, accessibility, valet parking, location, experience, what to expect); every service-specific question lives on that service's page"
    intent: >
      Clear away the practical worries that stop a first booking.
      Omit the truncated retinoids/Accutane entry wherever FAQs appear.
  - id: hours_location
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Answer "can I come after work?" with today's hours first.
      The full week: Mon–Fri 3:00 PM - 7:00 PM, Sat 11:00 AM - 5:00 PM, Sun 3:00 PM - 6:00 PM.
      Give the address exactly as written: 200 Columbus Blvd, 22nd Floor, Hartford, CT 06103.
      Note that valet parking is available and the studio is wheelchair accessible.
      No embedded map: the content has no coordinates.
  - id: contact
    priority: essential
    show: "phone and email inline plus a link to booking.html; the booking request form (form_type reservation, via the Kora forms API with reCAPTCHA) lives on booking.html"
    intent: >
      Make reaching her the easiest act on the page.
      The phone number is rendered exactly as +18608387039 and works as a tel: link.
      The email is facialsbyvanessact@gmail.com.

avoid:
  - "Rated 5★ by 65 reviewers", or any review count or average. Only the five reviews in the content exist here.
  - Reviewer profile photos from googleusercontent. They are not in the permitted image list.
  - '"10 years". The content says 9, and 9 is the only figure used.'
  - Deposit amounts ($95, $30) and the "Pay over time / 0% APR" banner from the old site.
  - Any mention of the Men Deluxe Facial, Brightening Pigment Peel, Anti-Acne Back Treatment, Deep Pore Cleansing Facial or Complete Skin Journey Program. None are offered in the content.
  - Inventing a price for ANTI-ACNE FACIAL TREATMENT or a duration for MICRODERMABRASION.
  - '"Our team", "trained professionals" or "clinicians". She works alone, and the copy says "I".'
  - Spa clichés such as orchids, candles, stacked stones, rolled towels, gold script or "indulge yourself" headlines.
  - Any serif face, and any weight above 400.
  - Drop shadows on anything. Depth comes from the tint bands, not from shadow.
  - A hero that states a philosophy ("your journey to radiance") instead of what she does.
  - Gold body text, or small text on gold panels. It fails contrast.
  - A scrolling marquee for the October availability note.
  - Star-rating rows and Google badges.
  - A blog or journal link. No blog exists on this site.
  - Labelling the services section "Menu".
  - Reformatting the phone number into (860) 838-7039. Render it exactly as +18608387039.
